Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to

Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 2001 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

PLIERS, BAR BENDING, DENTAL, 

WALDSACH'S TYPE 

(First Revision)

1.. Scope — Specifies material, dimensions and other requirements of bar bending pliers of Waldsach's 
type used in dentistry. 

2. Material — Stainless steel of designation 30Cr13 corforming to IS : 6603-1972' Specification for 
stainless steel bars and flats'. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1, 

3.1 Tolerances on linear dimensions shall be permitted as follows: 

a) ± O'l mm on dimensions up to 2"0 mm, 

b) ± 0*2 mm on dimensions above 20 mm and up to 5'0 mm, 

c) ± 0'5 mm on dimensions above 5*0 mm and up to 200 mm, 

d) ± VO mm on dimensions above 20'0 mm and up to 500 mm, 

e) ± 20 mm on dimensions above 500 mm and up to 1000 mm, and 

f) ± 2'5 mm on dimensions above 1000 mm. 

3.2 Tolerances on angular dimensions shall be ± 1**. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The two halves of the pliers shall move fully and freely at the joint without any play. The jaws 
shall register accurately on closing the pliers. 

4.2 The joint shall be flat box type conforming to 6 of IS : 3642-1978 'General requirements for 
surgical instruments ( fitst revision )'. The ends of the pin in the joint shall be finished flush Vvith the 
surface. 

4.3 The pliers shall be free from sharp edges, pits, burrs, cracks and other surface defects. All the 
edges except the working end shall be rounded. 

4.4 The surface of the pliers shall be finished smooth. 

4.5 The pliers shall be polished bright and passivated except the outside surface of the handle which 
may have a matt finish, by treating them in aJO percent {vlv) nitric acidjolution for not less than 
30 minutes at a temperature of not less than 10"t; and not exceeding 60"C. ihe pliers shall then be 
rinsed in water, dried in hot air and the joint lightly lubricated with a non-toxic and non-corrosive 
substance. 

5. Heat Treatment — The pliers shall be uniformly hardened and tempered to a hardness of 400 to 
4807/1/, when tested in accordance with IS : 1501-1968 'Method for vickers hardness test for steel 
{first revision )\ 

6. Tests 

6.1 Practical Test — The pliers shall be used to bend and shape a wire 1 mm in diameter and made 
of stainless steel of designation 04Cr18Ni10 or 07Cr18Ni9 of IS: 6528-1972 'Specification for 
stainless steel wire'. This shall be done six times. The pliers shall not show any sign of damage or 
acquire a permanent set after the test. 

6.2 Elasticity Test — The pliers shall be made to grip a piece of 1 mm thick hardened steel bit 
having a minimum hardress of 250 HV, A compressive force of 200 N ( 20 kgf approx) shall be applied 
to the pliers and allowed to act for 5 minutes in such a manner that the force acts on each arm of the 
handle [ a total of 400 N ( 40 kgf approx) on the instrument] at a distance of 40 mm from its free end. 
The pliers shall not show any 3ign Of damage or acquire a per.manent set after the test.

6.3 Corrosion Resistance Test — lhe pliers shall be tested in accordance with 15:7531-1975 
'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments'. 
It shall not show any sign of corrosion after the test. 

7. Marking — Each plier shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, initials 
or registered trade-mark, the words 'Staniess Steel', and the country of manufacture. 

7.1 IS! Certification Marl< — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — Each plier shall be wrapped either in a polyethylene bag or a wax paper. It shall then 
be packed in cartons in accordance with the current trade practice. The carton shall bear the name of 
the pliers, manufacturer's name, initials or registered trade-mark; the words 'Stainless Steel' and the 
country of manufacture. 

8.1 Alternatively, it may be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

9. Sannpling 

9,1 Sampling procedure and acceptance criteria for the plier shall be as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. A recommended scheme for the same is given in Appendix A. 

APPENDIX A 

( Clause 9.1 ) 

SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY FOR PLIERS, 
BAR BENDING, DENTAL, WALDSACH'S TYPE 

A-1 . Lot — In any consignment, all the pliers produced from the same material under similar conditions 
shall constitute a lot. 

A-2. The number of pliers to be selected from each lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall 
be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. 

TABLE 1 SAMPLIWG AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

Lot Size Sample Size 

(1) (2) 

Up to 15 2 

16 to 50 3 

51 to 150 5 

151 and above 8 

A-2.1 These pliers shall be selected from a lot at random and in order to ensure the randomness of 
selection, procedures given in IS : 4905-1968 'Methods for random sampling' may be followed. 

A-3. Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity — All the pliers selected at random in 
accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1 shall be tested for shape and dimensions, workmanship and 
finish, heat treatment, practical test, elasticity test, and corrosion resistance test. The lot shall be 
considered as conforming to these requirements if none of the pliers in the sample is found to be 
defective in any of these tests. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1967. The present revision has been undertaken to bring it 
in line with the current trade practices prevalent in the dental instruments industry. 

In this revision, tolerances on linear and angular dimensions, proper references to raw-materials 
and sampling plan have been specified. 



Printed at Printrade, New Delhi. India
